display.purpose: The single intro line. One per view.

headline.purpose: Section headings: results header, How it works.

title.purpose: Step headings inside How it works; footer wordmark.

body.purpose: Prose, subtitles, table cells, compact UI copy.

mono.purpose: Machine-produced strings: URLs, status codes, stat values, progress, limits, footer notes. Always tabular-nums.

shadows.name: panel-lift
shadows.purpose: The only shadow token (--shadow). Seats raised panels (form card, summary panel, table container, suggestion dropdown) on the ground. Ambient and soft.

shadows.name: focus-glow
shadows.purpose: Text-entry focus ring; pairs with an amber border shift in place of the global 2px amber outline.

motion.name: fade-in
motion.purpose: The single orchestrated entrance; results container only.

motion.name: progress-width
motion.purpose: Scan progress fill; also the health strip's width transition runs at 0.6s ease.

motion.name: spin
motion.purpose: Primary-button loading spinner while a scan runs.

motion.name: standard-ease
motion.purpose: State transitions: hover/focus colour, border, background changes.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Load-bearing accessibility switch; collapses the whole motion budget.

components.name: Primary Button
components.description: The one action per view: start the scan. Amber fill, ink label, 52px tall to match the URL field.

components.name: Secondary Outline Button
components.description: Export actions (JSON / CSV). Amber outline that inverts to full amber on hover.

components.name: Ghost Button
components.description: Quiet utility action (e.g. Unhide all). Hairline border, slate text, brightens on hover.
components.css: .ds-btn-ghost { height: 36px; padding: 0 0.8rem; background: transparent; border: 1px solid var(--border-strong, #32404f); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 6px); color: var(--text-secondary, #9daaba); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 550; cursor: pointer; transition: color 0.12s ease, border-color 0.12s ease; } .ds-btn-ghost:hover { color: var(--text, #e9edf2); border-color: var(--text-muted, #7c8b9b); } .ds-btn-ghost:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e5a33d); outline-offset: 2px; border-radius: 6px; }

components.name: URL Input
components.description: The dominant element of the page: monospace URL entry in a recessed well with a drawn link glyph and amber caret.
components.css: .ds-url-wrap { position: relative; } .ds-url-icon { position: absolute; left: 0.95rem; top: 50%; transform: translateY(-50%); width: 18px; height: 18px; color: var(--text-muted, #7c8b9b); pointer-events: none; } .ds-url-input { width: 100%; height: 52px; padding: 0 1rem 0 2.6rem; background: var(--surface-2, #1a222c); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong, #32404f); border-radius: var(--radius, 10px); color: var(--text, #e9edf2); font-family: ui-monospace, 'SF Mono', 'Cascadia Mono', Menlo, Consolas, monospace; font-size: 0.95rem; caret-color: var(--accent, #e5a33d); transition: border-color 0.15s ease, box-shadow 0.15s ease; } .ds-url-input::placeholder { color: var(--text-muted, #7c8b9b); font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; } .ds-url-input:focus { outline: none; border-color: var(--accent, #e5a33d); box-shadow: 0 0 0 3px rgba(229, 163, 61, 0.13); }

components.name: Segmented Filter
components.description: Link-type filter (All / Internal / External). Active segment is the one amber chip in the world.
components.css: .ds-segmented { display: inline-flex; background: var(--surface-2, #1a222c); border: 1px solid var(--border-strong, #32404f); border-radius: var(--radius-sm, 6px); padding: 3px; gap: 2px; } .ds-filter { padding: 0.32rem 0.75rem; border: none; background: transparent; color: var(--text-secondary, #9daaba); border-radius: 4px; cursor: pointer; font-family: -apple-system, BlinkMacSystemFont, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, sans-serif; font-size: 0.8rem; font-weight: 550; transition: background 0.12s ease, color 0.12s ease; } .ds-filter:hover { color: var(--text, #e9edf2); } .ds-filter.is-active { background: var(--accent, #e5a33d); color: var(--accent-ink, #191104); } .ds-filter:focus-visible { outline: 2px solid var(--accent, #e5a33d); outline-offset: 2px; }

narrative.overview:
A precision work surface for one job: paste a URL, watch the scan, work the dead-link list, export it. The world is a cool, dim ink ground lifted one tonal step at a time — panels, tracks, wells — never by decoration. There is exactly one voice of warmth: signal amber, spent on the things you can act on (the primary button, focus, selection, the active filter, key emphasis). Everything the machine produced reads as instrument output: URLs, status codes, counters, progress, and footnotes set in a monospace with tabular figures. Nothing here performs; it reports.

The build confirms the refusal stated up front. No purple-gradient SaaS template, no terminal-hacker costume, no hero-scale marketing type, no faux-proof. Density is moderate — one screen teaches the whole job — and the motion budget is nearly zero: a single orchestrated fade when results land, the progress bar's width transition, the health strip's width easing, and a spinner while scanning. Red and green exist only to say broken or working; they are never decoration.
keyCharacteristics: Cool dark ink ground; depth built from one-step-lighter panels and 1px hairline borders, plus a soft two-layer ambient shadow on raised panels
Warm off-white text, tinted slate greys for secondary and muted roles
A single signal-amber accent (#e5a33d) held in reserve for action and emphasis — rarity is the point
ui-monospace with tabular figures for everything machine-produced: URLs, status codes, stat values, progress readout, limits line, footer notes
Signature move: the full-width segmented link-health strip in the results summary — working vs broken share of checked links, encoded as data, not ornament
Drawn stroke SVG icons throughout; no emoji, no icon font, no raster imagery (favicon is an inline SVG data URI)
Browser surfaces themed: ::selection, :focus-visible, caret, webkit scrollbars, color-scheme: dark

rules.name: The One Signal Rule
rules.body: Amber is the only warm saturated hue on screen at rest, and it stays under roughly a tenth of any view. If amber appears twice in one glance, one of them is decoration — remove it.

rules.name: The State-Only Rule
rules.body: Red and green are reserved words. They mean broken and working. They never brand, decorate, or accent anything that is not a link's health, a destructive hover, or an error. The 404 badge is the single sanctioned exception: amber, because it is the most common finding and is treated as emphasis, not failure.

rules.name: The Warm-on-Cool Rule
rules.body: All text is warm-off-white on cool slate. Never introduce a pure white (#fff) or a blue-tinted text; the temperature split is the system's whole mood.

rules.name: The Readout Rule
rules.body: If a string was produced by the machine — a URL, an HTTP status, a count, a percentage, a timestamp, a limit — it is monospace with tabular figures. Sans never carries data.

rules.name: The One-Line Rule
rules.body: One heading level does one job: display introduces the tool, headline labels a section, title labels a step. No skipped levels, no display type below the intro.

rules.name: The One Canvas Rule
rules.body: One column, one width. No multi-column marketing layouts, no sidebars, no masonry — the tool is a single instrument panel.

rules.name: The One-Step Rule
rules.body: Depth is one tonal step and a hairline, everywhere. A surface rises by going lighter, never by gaining a stroke heavier than 1px (border-strong only for interactive affordance).

rules.name: The No-Hard-Shadow Rule
rules.body: No offset or hard-edged shadows anywhere. The world is a dim room, not a cut-paper collage.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Every boundary is a 1px hairline in Hairline or Strong Hairline; the only filled boundaries are amber (active filter segment) or the pill clips of data visualisation.

rules.name: The Pill-Is-Data Rule
rules.body: Fully rounded 999px shapes are reserved for data — progress, health strip, badges, dots, scrollbars — never for buttons. Buttons stay at 6–10px.

dos: Do spend amber only on the One Signal list: primary action, focus ring, selection, active filter, 404 badge, broken-link URLs, key emphasis. If it isn't one of those, it isn't amber.
Do set every machine-produced string in ui-monospace with font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums (The Readout Rule).
Do build depth from the tonal ladder + 1px hairlines; reach for --shadow only on raised panels and the suggestion dropdown (The One-Step Rule).
Do keep red and green strictly as broken/working state (The State-Only Rule) — including hovers on destructive controls.
Do keep :focus-visible as a 2px amber outline with 2px offset everywhere outside text-entry surfaces; keep color-scheme: dark, themed ::selection, amber caret, and webkit scrollbars as shipped.
Do respect prefers-reduced-motion: reduce — it is load-bearing, not decorative.
donts: Don't use amber as a decorative wash, gradient, or background block — there are no gradients anywhere in this world, and there shouldn't be.
Don't introduce a second accent hue, or promote red/green to brand colours.
Don't set data in the sans stack, or prose in the mono stack.
Don't add hard offset shadows, glows, or neobrutalist strokes — depth is tonal, and shadows are ambient and two-layer soft (The No-Hard-Shadow Rule).
Don't use emoji or icon fonts; icons are drawn 1.7–1.8 stroke-width SVG, aria-hidden, sized 15–34px.
Don't add a second breakpoint or reflow the results table into cards; below 860px it scrolls horizontally inside its container.
Don't invent proof — no user counts, testimonials, uptime claims, or certifications anywhere in this world.
